summary: Böckle, Iyengar and Paškūnas determine the geometry of the unrestricted framed deformation ring R^□_ρ̄ of any ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k), for every finite F/Q_p and every d. It is a local complete intersection, flat over O, of relative dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p], so every ρ̄ lifts to characteristic zero, absolutely irreducibly (Theorem 1.1). Its irreducible components are the Spec R^{□,χ}_ρ̄, indexed by characters χ of μ_{p^∞}(F) through R_{det ρ̄} → R^□_ρ̄, which is flat; each R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ is a normal complete-intersection domain, and they are factorial for absolutely irreducible ρ̄ except when d = 2, F = Q_3, ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄(1) (Theorems 1.2 and 1.4, Corollary 1.3). The fixed-determinant rings R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ are normal complete-intersection domains (Theorem 1.5), and for p ∤ 2d the crystalline, potentially crystabelline and potentially crystalline supercuspidal points are Zariski dense (Theorem 1.6). The method: the generic-matrices space X^gen over the pseudodeformation space X^ps, GIT over a base (Seshadri), fibre-dimension bounds from local duality, and Böckle–Juschka's equidimensionality of R^ps/ϖ give dim X̄^gen ≤ d² + d²[F:Q_p]. Completions at closed points identify local rings of X^gen with framed rings over local fields, and density of the Kummer-irreducible and absolutely irreducible loci with codimension bounds gives normality by Serre's criterion. The density theorem combines the components with the patched module of CEGGPS and Emerton–Paškūnas. In the atlas, LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 plans the unrestricted rings but none of these theorems, and no layer plans the CEGGPS module. The paper's own theory therefore becomes a Part II of LocalGaloisDeformationRings, and §6 a Part II of CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility in the direction of R31.5. General inputs go as sources to R08.1, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3, IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1, ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 and PadicHodgeTheory R06.2. Seven misprints and two errors are recorded: the proof of Lemma 6.5 needs an unramified twist, and some numerical bounds need d ≥ 2. No stated result is affected.

items.name: Seshadri's setting: a reductive group scheme acting on a closed invariant subscheme of affine space, and its GIT quotient
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring, S = Spec R and G a reductive group scheme over S (an affine group scheme, smooth over S, with connected reductive geometric fibres; in the application G = GL_d or G_m^r over S). Let V be a free R-module of finite rank r with a G-module structure, V̌ = Hom_R(V, R), and X a closed G-invariant subscheme of Spec Sym(V̌) = A^r_S, with ring of functions B. The GIT quotient X//G is Spec B^G, and for a geometric point y = Spec κ of X//G the fibre X_y is identified with a closed G-invariant subscheme of X.
items.note: Seshadri, Geometric reductivity over arbitrary base (1977). LanglandsParameterStacks LP2:integral-invariants and LP3 plan reductive invariant theory for Weil-group parameters with ℓ ≠ p (FS VIII), not Seshadri's theory over an arbitrary Noetherian base; the Part II should share the GL_d case with LP3 where the hypotheses allow.

items.name: Seshadri: unique closed orbit in each geometric fibre of X → X//G, and closedness of images of invariant closed sets
items.statement: In the setting of item 001: (1) for every geometric point y of X//G, the fibre X_y contains a unique closed G-orbit, and so does every closed G-invariant subscheme of X_y (Seshadri, Theorem 3); (2) the image in X//G of a closed G-invariant subset of X is closed (Seshadri, Corollary 2(ii) to Proposition 9).
items.locator: Used in the proofs of Lemma 2.2, p. 8, Lemma 3.7, p. 12 and Lemma 3.21, p. 17 (arXiv v2 pp. 9, 14, 20)
items.note: Imported from Seshadri (1977); a prerequisite paper, not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: irreducible components of X are G-invariant
items.statement: In the setting of item 001, every irreducible component Z of X, with its reduced subscheme structure, is G-invariant: the action map G ×_S X → X carries G ×_S Z into Z.
items.note: Proof: for Z = V(𝔭), the kernel of B → O(G) ⊗_R B/𝔭 is contained in 𝔭, and O(G) ⊗_R B/𝔭 is a domain because G → S is smooth with geometrically integral fibres, so the kernel is a prime contained in the minimal prime 𝔭.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: the dimension of a GIT fibre is bounded by a tangent space at a point of its closed orbit
items.statement: In the setting of item 001, let y = Spec κ be a geometric point of X//G and x ∈ X_y(κ) a point whose orbit G·x is closed in X_y. Then dim X_y ≤ dim_κ T_x(X_y).

items.name: Framed deformation functor and framed deformation ring R^□_ρ̄
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. D^□_ρ̄: 𝔄_O → Sets sends a local Artinian O-algebra (A, 𝔪_A) with residue field k to the set of continuous representations ρ_A: G_F → GL_d(A) with ρ_A mod 𝔪_A = ρ̄; it is pro-represented by a complete local Noetherian O-algebra R^□_ρ̄.
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 plans framed local representability; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.2 the representability criteria.

items.name: Mazur's presentation of R^□_ρ̄ and the local Euler characteristic count
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. Writing h^i = dim_k H^i(G_F, ad ρ̄), the tangent space of D^□_ρ̄ is Z^1(G_F, ad ρ̄) and there is a presentation R^□_ρ̄ ≅ O⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧/(f_1, …, f_s) with r = dim_k Z^1(G_F, ad ρ̄) = d² − h^0 + h^1 and s = h^2; the local Euler–Poincaré characteristic formula gives r − s = d² + d²[F:Q_p].
items.locator: §3, (4) and the paragraph after it, p. 8 (arXiv v2 p. 10)
items.note: From Mazur's Deforming Galois representations §1.6 and An introduction to the deformation theory of Galois representations Proposition 21.1. R08.1 plans the tangent/obstruction description; Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans finiteness of local cohomology with finite coefficients and the local Euler characteristic.

items.name: Complete intersection from the dimension bounds (3)
items.statement: Let Λ be a complete regular local ring (here O or a complete DVR), R = Λ⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧/(f_1, …, f_s) and π a regular parameter of Λ. If dim R ≤ dim Λ⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧ − s and dim R/π ≤ dim Λ⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧ − s − 1, then π, f_1, …, f_s extend to a system of parameters of the regular ring Λ⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧ and hence form a regular sequence; so R and R/π are complete intersections of dimensions dim Λ⟦x⟧ − s and dim Λ⟦x⟧ − s − 1, and R is π-torsion free. For R = R^□_ρ̄ the bounds (3) are dim R^□_ρ̄ ≤ 1 + d² + d²[F:Q_p] and dim R^□_ρ̄/ϖ ≤ d² + d²[F:Q_p].
items.locator: §3, (3) and the paragraph after (4), p. 8 (arXiv v2 p. 10); used again in Corollary 3.38 and Proposition 4.3
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 plans regular sequences, Cohen–Macaulay rings and 'the exact complete-intersection criteria used in patching'; its reviewed audit (data/library-coverage.json) records regular sequences in Mathlib (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular, Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/RegularSequence.lean:146) and no Cohen–Macaulay or complete-intersection predicate in either library.

items.name: Pseudo-characters (determinant laws), the pseudo-character D̄ of ρ̄, and the universal pseudodeformation ring R^ps
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. A d-dimensional pseudo-character of A[G_F] is a determinant law in Chenevier's sense: a multiplicative A-polynomial law A[G_F] → A, homogeneous of degree d. D̄: k[G_F] → k is the composite of the polynomial laws of ρ̄: k[G_F] → M_d(k) and det. D^ps: 𝔄_O → Sets sends A to the set of continuous d-dimensional A-valued pseudo-characters of A[G_F] reducing to D̄; it is pro-represented by a complete local Noetherian O-algebra (R^ps, 𝔪_{R^ps}) (Chenevier, Proposition 3.3), with universal pseudo-character D^u: R^ps⟦G_F⟧ → R^ps. Sending a deformation of ρ̄ to its determinant gives R^ps → R^□_ρ̄.
items.note: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0 plans polynomial laws and determinants with their continuity criteria; GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1 plans 'a separate determinant/pseudorepresentation deformation functor'. Mathlib has PolynomialLaw (Mathlib/RingTheory/PolynomialLaw/Basic.lean:77) but no multiplicative or determinant laws. The paper follows Chenevier's convention that the pseudo-character of a direct sum is the product.

items.name: Böckle–Juschka (Theorem 1.8): R^ps/ϖ is equidimensional of dimension 1 + d²[F:Q_p]; the special locus is small
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. (1) R^ps/ϖ is equidimensional of dimension 1 + d²[F:Q_p] (Böckle–Juschka, Theorem 5.5.1(a) in Theorem 1.8 and 5.4.1(a) in §§3.4 and 3.7). (2) The Zariski closure in X̄^ps = Spec R^ps/ϖ of the special absolutely irreducible locus U^spcl (item 063) has dimension at most 1 + ½[F:Q_p]d². (3) The same results for each universal deformation ring R^ps_j of a factor D̄'_j of D̄, which give dim R^ps_j/ϖ = 1 + d_j²[F:Q_p].
items.locator: Theorem 1.8, p. 4 (arXiv v2 p. 4); used in (17) and (19), p. 20, and the proofs of Lemma 3.52 and Proposition A.9
items.note: Imported from Böckle–Juschka, Forum Math. Sigma 11 (2023) e102; a prerequisite paper, not in the atlas. It is the only input on R^ps in characteristic p, and the whole dimension count of §3.4 rests on it.

items.name: Cayley–Hamilton algebras, the Cayley–Hamilton quotient E = R^ps⟦G_F⟧/CH(D^u), and homomorphisms of Cayley–Hamilton algebras
items.statement: Let CH(D^u) be the Cayley–Hamilton ideal of R^ps⟦G_F⟧ (Chenevier §1.17), the closed two-sided ideal such that E := R^ps⟦G_F⟧/CH(D^u) is the largest quotient on which the Cayley–Hamilton theorem for D^u holds (a Cayley–Hamilton R^ps-algebra of degree d). For a commutative R^ps-algebra B, an R^ps-algebra homomorphism f: E → M_d(B) is a homomorphism of Cayley–Hamilton algebras if det ∘ f equals the specialisation of D^u along R^ps → B. For y: R^ps → κ, E_y := E ⊗_{R^ps,y} κ ≅ (R^ps⟦G_F⟧ ⊗_{R^ps,y} κ)/CH(D_y) (Chenevier §1.22; Wang-Erickson's thesis, Lemma 1.1.8.6).
items.note: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1 plans 'the characteristic-polynomial ideal and Cayley–Hamilton quotient'.

items.name: E is a finitely generated R^ps-module
items.statement: The Cayley–Hamilton quotient E = R^ps⟦G_F⟧/CH(D^u) of item 010 is a finitely generated R^ps-module (Wang-Erickson, Proposition 3.6). Consequently E_y is a finite-dimensional κ-algebra for every y: R^ps → κ.
items.note: Imported from Wang-Erickson, Math. Ann. 371 (2018); it uses Mazur's p-finiteness of G_F. IHG.1 does not state finiteness of Cayley–Hamilton quotients of completed group algebras.

items.name: Lemma 3.1: the algebra of generic matrices A^gen (Procesi)
items.statement: There is a finitely generated commutative R^ps-algebra A^gen with a homomorphism of Cayley–Hamilton R^ps-algebras j: E → M_d(A^gen) such that for every commutative R^ps-algebra B and every homomorphism of Cayley–Hamilton R^ps-algebras f: E → M_d(B) there is a unique R^ps-algebra map f̃: A^gen → B with f = M_d(f̃) ∘ j. Concretely A^gen = C/I, where C, a quotient of R^ps ⊗_Z Sym(W) with W a sum of n copies of End(Std)^*, represents R^ps-algebra maps E → M_d(B) (n the size of a generating set of E), and I is generated by Λ_i(a) − c_i(j(a)) for a ∈ E and 0 ≤ i ≤ d, where D^u(t − a) = Σ_{i=0}^{d} (−1)^i Λ_i(a) t^{d−i} and c_i are the characteristic-polynomial coefficients.
items.locator: Lemma 3.1, p. 9 (arXiv v2 p. 10); Remark 3.5, p. 11
items.note: Procesi, A formal inverse to the Cayley–Hamilton theorem (1987); Wang-Erickson, Theorem 3.8 (X^gen ≅ Rep^□_{E,D^u}). The statement is corrected for source issue E1 (the printed sum runs to n). Remark 3.5 shows the Cayley–Hamilton condition is needed: without it a specialisation of E → M_2 can have pseudo-character χ_1 + χ_1 when D̄ = χ_1 + χ_2.

items.name: Chenevier: characteristic polynomials determine a determinant law, and semisimple reconstruction over algebraically closed fields
items.statement: (1) A d-dimensional determinant law D is determined by the coefficients of its characteristic polynomials D(t − a) (Chenevier, Corollary 1.14; Wang-Erickson's thesis 1.1.9.15); in particular the coefficients of D^u(t − a) generate a dense O-subalgebra of R^ps, and likewise for each R^ps_j. (2) Over an algebraically closed field κ every d-dimensional determinant law D of G_F is the determinant of a semisimple representation G_F → GL_d(κ), unique up to isomorphism, and D = ∏ D_i with D_i irreducible (Chenevier, Theorem 2.12). (3) If D̄ is multiplicity free, E is a generalised matrix algebra (Chenevier, Theorem 2.22).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 3.1, p. 9, and Lemma 3.24, p. 19; §3.2, p. 11; proof of Corollary 4.28, p. 41 (arXiv v2 pp. 11, 13, 21, 46)
items.note: IHG.1 plans 'reconstruction over algebraically closed fields up to semisimplification' and generalised matrix algebra decompositions under residually multiplicity-free hypotheses; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.6 records a related node (Chenevier's Theorem B) in its integrated decomposition.

items.name: The spaces X^gen = Spec A^gen and X^ps = Spec R^ps, the conjugation action of GL_d, and their special fibres
items.statement: GL_d acts on W by conjugation, hence on X^gen := Spec A^gen: a point of X^gen(B) is an n-tuple of d × d matrices over B satisfying the relations of A^gen, and GL_d(B) conjugates them. X^gen is isomorphic to Wang-Erickson's Rep^□_{E,D^u}. The GIT quotient X^gen//GL_d = Spec (A^gen)^{GL_d} receives R^ps → (A^gen)^{GL_d}, giving X^gen → X^ps := Spec R^ps; X̄^gen and X̄^ps are the special fibres. R^ps is given its 𝔪_{R^ps}-adic topology, for which it is compact.

items.name: X^gen//GL_d → X^ps is an adequate homeomorphism (Wang-Erickson, Alper)
items.statement: The map X^gen//GL_d → X^ps, and likewise X̄^gen//GL_d → X̄^ps, is an adequate homeomorphism in Alper's sense (Definition 3.3.1): an integral universal homeomorphism which is a local isomorphism around points with residue field of characteristic zero (Wang-Erickson, Theorem 2.20). Consequently (Alper, Proposition 3.3.5) the kernel of R^ps → (A^gen)^{GL_d} is nilpotent and vanishes after inverting p.
items.locator: §3.1, (5), p. 9 (arXiv v2 p. 11); proof of Corollary 4.28, p. 41 (arXiv v2 p. 46)
items.note: Imported from Wang-Erickson (2018) and Alper, Adequate moduli spaces (2014); prerequisite papers.

items.name: Lemma 3.2: every R^ps-algebra map E → M_d(B) gives a continuous representation
items.statement: Let B be a topological R^ps-algebra. If f: E → M_d(B) is any (not a priori continuous) homomorphism of R^ps-algebras, then G_F → E^× → GL_d(B) is a continuous representation.

items.name: Lemma 3.3: R^ps[G_F] → E is surjective
items.statement: The composition R^ps[G_F] → R^ps⟦G_F⟧ ↠ E is surjective.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: closed points of X^gen over the closed point of X^ps have pseudo-character D̄
items.statement: Let x be a closed point of X^gen above the closed point of X^ps and ρ_x: G_F → GL_d(κ(x)) the composite of G_F → R^ps⟦G_F⟧ → E → M_d(A^gen) → M_d(κ(x)). Then the pseudo-character of ρ_x is D̄ ⊗_k κ(x); in particular ρ_x and ρ̄ ⊗_k κ(x) have the same semisimplification.

items.name: Fibres X^gen_y, the decomposition D_y = ∏ D_i, twist classes, and the block parabolic P ⊃ N, L, Z_L with ρ_σ
items.statement: Let 𝔭 ⊂ R^ps be prime with dim R^ps/𝔭 ≤ 1, κ an algebraic closure of κ(𝔭) with its natural topology, y: R^ps → κ, and X^gen_y := X^gen ×_{X^ps,y} Spec κ. Write D_y = ∏_{i=1}^r D_i with D_i irreducible of dimension d_i, fix ρ_i: G_F → GL_{d_i}(κ) with pseudo-character D_i, and set D_i ~ D_j if D_i = D_j(m) for some m ∈ Z; let k be the number of classes and n_i the size of the i-th. For σ ∈ S_r let P be the block upper triangular parabolic with i-th diagonal block of size d_{σ(i)}, N its unipotent radical, L its block-diagonal Levi, Z_L ≅ G_m^r its centre, 𝔭, 𝔫, 𝔩, 𝔷_L, 𝔤𝔩_d the Lie algebras (dim 𝔫 = Σ_{i<j} d_i d_j, independent of σ by Remark 3.8), and ρ_σ = diag(ρ_{σ(1)}, …, ρ_{σ(r)}). 𝔭 is a Cayley–Hamilton subalgebra of M_d(κ).

items.name: Lemma 3.6: Hom and Ext^1 over E_y agree with those over G_F between distinct factors
items.statement: In the setting of item 019, for i ≠ j, Hom_{E_y}(ρ_i, ρ_j) = Hom_{G_F}(ρ_i, ρ_j) and Ext^1_{E_y}(ρ_i, ρ_j) = Ext^1_{G_F}(ρ_i, ρ_j), the latter computed among continuous representations of G_F on finite-dimensional κ-vector spaces.
items.note: The footnote records that the statement can fail for i = j (V irreducible gives E_y = M_d(κ) but Ext^1_{G_F}(ρ_1, ρ_1) ≠ 0).

items.name: Lemma 3.7: X^gen_y is connected, its closed orbit is the semisimple locus, and its dimension when the ρ_i are distinct
items.statement: The fibre X^gen_y is connected and its unique closed GL_d-orbit consists of the semisimple representations. If the ρ_i are pairwise non-isomorphic, this orbit has dimension d² − r.

items.name: Lemma 3.9: the closed subscheme X^gen_{y,σ} of block upper triangular representations
items.statement: There is a closed subscheme X^gen_{y,σ} ⊂ X^gen_y representing the functor sending a κ-algebra B to the set of homomorphisms of Cayley–Hamilton κ-algebras φ: E_y → 𝔭 ⊗_κ B whose projection to the i-th diagonal block is ρ_{σ(i)} ⊗_κ B for 1 ≤ i ≤ r.

items.name: Lemma 3.10: the unique closed Z_L-orbit in X^gen_{y,σ} is {ρ_σ}
items.statement: The unique closed Z_L-orbit in X^gen_{y,σ} is the singleton {ρ_σ}.

items.name: Local Tate duality and the Euler–Poincaré formula for finite and p-adic coefficients
items.statement: Let κ be a finite extension of k or a finite extension of L, and V a continuous representation of G_F on a finite-dimensional κ-vector space. Then H^i(G_F, V) is finite-dimensional, vanishes for i > 2, H^2(G_F, V) is dual to H^0(G_F, V^*(1)), and Σ_i (−1)^i dim_κ H^i(G_F, V) = −[F:Q_p] dim_κ V.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.11, p. 14; (22), p. 23; proofs of Lemmas 4.11–4.12, p. 37 (arXiv v2 pp. 16, 26, 41–42); Böckle–Juschka, Theorem 3.4.1(b)(c)
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans local duality and the Euler characteristic for finite modules; ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 plans local duality for compact (lattice) coefficients, from which the case of a finite extension of L follows.

items.name: Local Tate duality and the Euler–Poincaré formula with coefficients in a local field of characteristic p
items.statement: Let κ be a local field of characteristic p containing k (so O_κ ≅ k'⟦t⟧), and V a continuous representation of G_F on a finite-dimensional κ-vector space. Then H^i(G_F, V) is finite-dimensional over κ, vanishes for i > 2, H^2(G_F, V) is dual to H^0(G_F, V^*(1)), and Σ_i (−1)^i dim_κ H^i(G_F, V) = −[F:Q_p] dim_κ V (Böckle–Juschka, Theorem 3.4.1, via Nekovář's Selmer complexes).
items.locator: Footnote to the proof of Proposition 3.11, p. 14 (arXiv v2 p. 16); (22), p. 23; Remark 4.7, p. 36
items.note: The case needed at closed points of X^gen with residue field a local field of characteristic p. D7's finite, compact and discrete regimes do not include k'⟦t⟧-lattices with t inverted.

items.name: Proposition 3.11: the tangent space of X^gen_{y,σ} at ρ_σ
items.statement: Let x ∈ X^gen_{y,σ} be the point of ρ_σ. Then dim T_x(X^gen_{y,σ}) = dim 𝔫 + (dim 𝔫)[F:Q_p] + Σ_{1≤i<j≤r} dim Hom_{G_F}(ρ_{σ(i)}, ρ_{σ(j)}(1)) ≤ dim 𝔫 + (dim 𝔫)[F:Q_p] + Σ_{i=1}^{k} (n_i choose 2).
items.locator: Proposition 3.11, p. 13 (arXiv v2 p. 15); Remark 3.12 (sharp when char κ = p and ζ_p ∈ F)
items.note: Proof: identify T_x with Z^1-type data of Hom and Ext^1 between the blocks via Lemma 3.6, then apply the Euler characteristic and local duality (items 024, 025).

items.name: Corollary 3.13: dimension bound for X^gen_{y,σ}
items.statement: dim X^gen_{y,σ} ≤ dim_κ T_x(X^gen_{y,σ}) ≤ dim 𝔫 + (dim 𝔫)[F:Q_p] + Σ_{i=1}^{k} (n_i choose 2).

items.name: Lemma 3.14: dominant finite type maps of Noetherian Jacobson universally catenary schemes do not raise dimension
items.statement: If f: X → Y is a dominant morphism of finite type between Noetherian Jacobson universally catenary schemes, then dim Y ≤ dim X.
items.note: Neither library defines catenary or Jacobson schemes (Mathlib has IsJacobsonRing, Mathlib/RingTheory/Jacobson/Ring.lean:60, for rings); the R03.3 audit records catenarity as absent.

items.name: Proposition 3.15: bound for the dimension of the fibres X^gen_y
items.statement: dim X^gen_y ≤ dim 𝔤𝔩_d − r + (dim 𝔫)[F:Q_p] + Σ_{i=1}^{k} (n_i choose 2).

items.name: Corollary 3.16: fibres over absolutely irreducible points are smooth of dimension d² − 1
items.statement: If r = 1 then X^gen_y is smooth of dimension dim 𝔤𝔩_d − 1 = d² − 1.

items.name: Lemma 3.17: residue fields and topology at primes of coheight one in a complete local O-algebra
items.statement: Let (R, 𝔪_R) be a complete local Noetherian O-algebra with finite residue field k' and P_1R = {𝔭 ∈ Spec R : dim R/𝔭 = 1}. If 𝔭 ∈ P_1R then κ(𝔭) is either a finite extension of L or a local field of characteristic p; R/𝔭 is contained in the ring of integers O_{κ(𝔭)}, and the quotient topology on R/𝔭 from the 𝔪_R-adic topology coincides with the subspace topology from O_{κ(𝔭)}.

items.name: Lemma 3.18(1)–(4): Jacobson property and closed points over the punctured spectrum of a complete local ring
items.statement: Let (R, 𝔪_R) be a complete local Noetherian ring, φ: R → S of finite type, U a non-empty open subscheme of U_max := Spec R ∖ {𝔪_R}, V and V_max the preimages of U and U_max in Spec S. Then (1) V is Jacobson; (2) the closed points of V are V ∩ {closed points of V_max}; (3) a closed point x of V maps to a closed point y of U with κ(x)/κ(y) finite; (4) the closed points of U are U ∩ P_1R.
items.note: Part (1) uses that the punctured spectrum of a Noetherian local ring is Jacobson (Stacks 02IM) and that finite type over Jacobson is Jacobson (Mathlib: RingHom.FiniteType.isJacobsonRing, Mathlib/RingTheory/Jacobson/Ring.lean:671, for rings only; the scheme version is missing).

items.name: Lemma 3.18(5)–(6): dimension of closures and fibre dimension bound over the punctured spectrum
items.statement: In the setting of item 032 let Z be the closure of V in Spec S and Y the preimage of {𝔪_R}. (5) If every irreducible component of Spec S meets Y, then dim Z = dim V + 1. (6) dim V ≤ dim U + max_{y ∈ U ∩ P_1R} dim φ^{−1}({y}).
items.locator: Lemma 3.18, p. 16 (arXiv v2 p. 18); parts (5)–(6); Remarks 3.19–3.20, p. 17
items.note: Remark 3.19 (R = Z_p, S = Z_p[x]/(px − 1) = Q_p) shows the hypothesis in (5) is needed; Remark 3.20 (S = Z_p[x], 𝔮 = (px − 1) versus (p, x)) shows that closed points of an irreducible such Spec S can have local rings of different dimensions, and that a closed point of Spec S need not lie over the closed point of Spec R. Both are acceptance tests.

items.name: Lemma 3.21: invariant closed subschemes meet the special fibre, and local dimensions at their closed points
items.statement: Let Y be the preimage of {𝔪_{R^ps}} in X^gen, W a non-empty closed GL_d-invariant subscheme of X^gen and Z an irreducible component of W. Then Y ∩ Z ≠ ∅, and for a closed point x of Z: (1) if x ∈ Y then dim O_{Z,x} = dim Z; (2) if x ∉ Y then dim O_{Z,x} = dim Z − 1.
items.locator: Lemma 3.21, p. 17 (arXiv v2 p. 20); Example 3.22, p. 17
items.note: The arXiv v2 comment says this lemma has a better proof, following the referee. Example 3.22 (Γ = Z_p, d = 2, ρ(γ) = (1 p^{−1}; 0 1)) exhibits a closed point of X^gen with residue field L not above the closed point of X^ps.

items.name: Lemma 3.23 (with Theorem 1.9): the generic fibre is no bigger than the special fibre
items.statement: Let W be a non-empty closed GL_d-invariant subscheme of X^gen with generic fibre W[1/p] and special fibre W̄. Then dim W[1/p] ≤ dim W̄; in particular dim X^gen[1/p] ≤ dim X̄^gen.
items.locator: Lemma 3.23, p. 18 (arXiv v2 p. 20); Theorem 1.9, p. 4

items.name: Partitions 𝒫 of the factors of D̄, the rings R^ps_Σ and R^{ps,ij}_Σ, and the strata X̄^ps_𝒫, U_𝒫, V_𝒫, Z_𝒫
items.statement: Write D̄ = ∏_{i=1}^m D̄_i with D̄_i absolutely irreducible. For an unordered partition 𝒫 of {1, …, m} into r parts and an ordering Σ = (Σ_1, …, Σ_r), let D̄'_j = ∏_{i∈Σ_j} D̄_i of dimension d_j, and group the D̄'_j into k' twist classes (D̄'_j ~ D̄'_{j'} if D̄'_j = D̄'_{j'}(t), t ∈ Z) of sizes n'_i and dimensions c_i; put l_𝒫 = Σ_j d_j², n_𝒫 = ½(d² − l_𝒫) = Σ_{j<j'} d_j d_{j'} and p_𝒫 = l_𝒫 + n_𝒫. Let R^ps_j be the universal deformation ring of D̄'_j and R^ps_Σ = R^ps_1 ⊗̂_O ⋯ ⊗̂_O R^ps_r, which represents ordered r-tuples of deformations; the product map gives ι_Σ: X̄^ps_Σ = Spec R^ps_Σ/ϖ → X̄^ps, whose scheme-theoretic image X̄^ps_𝒫 depends only on 𝒫. Order partitions by refinement (𝒫_min has one part, 𝒫_max has m parts); U_𝒫 := X̄^ps_𝒫 ∖ ({𝔪_{R^ps}} ∪ ⋃_{𝒫<𝒫'} X̄^ps_{𝒫'}), V_𝒫 its preimage in X̄^gen and Z_𝒫 the closure of V_𝒫. For i ≠ j, R^{ps,ij}_Σ is the quotient of R^ps_Σ where D_i = D_j(1), X̄^{ps,ij}_𝒫 its image, U^{ij}_𝒫 = U_𝒫 ∩ X̄^{ps,ij}_𝒫, and V^{ij}_𝒫, Z^{ij}_𝒫 as before.
items.note: Corrected for source issue E2 (the printed definition reads X^ps_j := R^ps_j).

items.name: Lemma 3.24: R^ps → R^ps_Σ is finite
items.statement: The map R^ps → R^ps_Σ is finite.
items.note: Proof: by topological Nakayama it suffices that k ⊗_{R^ps} R^ps_Σ is Artinian; a coheight-one prime would give a factor D_{i,y} with transcendental characteristic-polynomial coefficients whose product is D̄ ⊗ κ, contradicting integrality over k.

items.name: Dimensions of the strata X̄^ps_𝒫 and X̄^{ps,ij}_𝒫, and the decomposition of X̄^gen_𝒫
items.statement: dim X̄^ps_𝒫 = dim X̄^ps_Σ = Σ_{i=1}^r dim X̄^ps_i = r + l_𝒫[F:Q_p]; if D̄'_i = D̄'_j(1) then dim X̄^{ps,ij}_𝒫 ≤ r + l_𝒫[F:Q_p] − (1 + [F:Q_p]) (and R^{ps,ij}_Σ = 0 otherwise). Every irreducible component of the preimage X̄^gen_𝒫 of X̄^ps_𝒫 in X̄^gen contains a closed point over 𝔪_{R^ps}, so dim Z_𝒫 = dim V_𝒫 + 1, and X̄^gen_𝒫 = Y ∪ ⋃_{𝒫≤𝒫'} Z_{𝒫'} with Y the preimage of {𝔪_{R^ps}}.
items.note: Combines Lemma 3.24, Böckle–Juschka (item 009) applied to each factor, Lemma 3.21 and Lemma 3.18(5).

items.name: Lemma 3.25: fibre dimension over the stratum U_𝒫
items.statement: If y is a geometric closed point of U_𝒫 then dim X^gen_y ≤ d² − r + n_𝒫[F:Q_p] + Σ_{i=1}^{k'} (n'_i choose 2); if moreover y ∉ U^{ij}_𝒫 for all i ≠ j, then dim X^gen_y ≤ d² − r + n_𝒫[F:Q_p].

items.name: Proposition 3.26: dimension of Z^{ij}_𝒫
items.statement: dim Z^{ij}_𝒫 ≤ d² + p_𝒫[F:Q_p] + Σ_{i=1}^{k'} (n'_i choose 2) − (1 + [F:Q_p]).

items.name: Proposition 3.27: dimension of Z_𝒫
items.statement: Let δ_𝒫 = max{0, Σ_{i=1}^{k'} (n'_i choose 2) − (1 + [F:Q_p])}. Then dim Z_𝒫 ≤ d² + p_𝒫[F:Q_p] + δ_𝒫.

items.name: Proposition 3.28: dimension of the absolutely irreducible stratum
items.statement: dim Z_{𝒫_min} ≤ d² + d²[F:Q_p].

items.name: Lemma 3.29: codimension of the reducible strata
items.statement: Assume 𝒫 ≠ 𝒫_min. If d = 2 then d² + d²[F:Q_p] − dim Z_𝒫 ≥ [F:Q_p]; otherwise d² + d²[F:Q_p] − dim Z_𝒫 ≥ 1 + [F:Q_p].

items.name: Lemma 3.30: dimension of the fibre Y over the closed point of X^ps
items.statement: Let Y be the preimage of {𝔪_{R^ps}} in X̄^gen. Then dim Y ≤ d² + n_{𝒫_max}[F:Q_p] + n_{𝒫_max} − 1; in particular d² + d²[F:Q_p] − dim Y ≥ 1 + l_{𝒫_max}[F:Q_p], which is ≥ 1 + 2[F:Q_p] when d ≥ 2.
items.note: Corrected for source issue E9: the printed final inequality ≥ 1 + 2[F:Q_p] needs l_{𝒫_max} ≥ 2, which fails for d = 1 (then X̄^gen = X̄^ps and the codimension of Y is 1 + [F:Q_p]); every use has d ≥ 2 or needs only positive codimension.

items.name: Theorem 3.31 (with Theorem 1.9): dim X̄^gen ≤ d² + d²[F:Q_p]
items.statement: dim X̄^gen ≤ d² + d²[F:Q_p]; together with Lemma 3.23, dim X^gen[1/p] ≤ dim X̄^gen ≤ d² + d²[F:Q_p].
items.locator: Theorem 3.31, p. 22 (arXiv v2 p. 24); Theorem 1.9, p. 4
items.note: The key dimension bound: X̄^gen = Y ∪ ⋃_𝒫 Z_𝒫, bounded by Lemma 3.30 and Propositions 3.27–3.28.

items.name: Coefficient rings Λ for residue fields that are finite or local fields, O-Cohen rings, and D^□_ρ on 𝔄_Λ
items.statement: Let ρ: G_F → GL_d(κ) be continuous, with κ a finite extension of k, a finite extension of L, or a local field of characteristic p containing k. Put (1) Λ = O_{L'} with L'/L unramified with residue field κ, if κ is finite; (2) Λ = κ, Λ^0 = O_κ, t = ϖ, if κ is a finite extension of L; (3) if κ is a local field of characteristic p with O_κ ≅ k'⟦t⟧, Λ^0 = O_{L'}⟦t⟧ (L'/L unramified with residue field k') and Λ the p-adic completion of Λ^0[1/t], a complete DVR with uniformiser ϖ and residue field κ (an O-Cohen ring of κ; any O-algebra that is a complete DVR with uniformiser ϖ and residue field κ is non-canonically isomorphic to Λ, Remark 3.32). 𝔄_Λ is the category of local Artinian Λ-algebras with residue field κ, topologised discretely in case (1), p-adically in case (2), and as finite-length Λ^0[1/t]/ϖ^n-modules in case (3); D^□_ρ(A) is the set of continuous ρ_A: G_F → GL_d(A) lifting ρ.
items.note: Remark 3.32 cites Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative IX §2.3 Proposition 4 for the uniqueness of O-Cohen rings.

items.name: Proposition 3.33 (with Remark 4.4): representability of D^□_ρ over Λ and its presentation
items.statement: In the setting of item 046, D^□_ρ: 𝔄_Λ → Sets is pro-represented by a complete local Noetherian Λ-algebra R^□_ρ with a presentation R^□_ρ ≅ Λ⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧/(f_1, …, f_s), r = dim_κ Z^1(G_F, ad ρ), s = dim_κ H^2(G_F, ad ρ); by the Euler–Poincaré formula in all three settings, r − s = d² + d²[F:Q_p]. The analogous presentation over R_{det ρ} (Proposition 4.3) holds for ρ over a local field κ (Remark 4.4), the continuous set-theoretic section of GL_d(R_u) → GL_d(R^□_ρ) being the extra input.
items.locator: Proposition 3.33, p. 23 (arXiv v2 p. 26); (21)–(22), p. 23; Remark 4.4, p. 35
items.note: For κ finite this is Mazur's obstruction theory, planned in R08.1 (item 006); for κ a local field the continuity of the obstruction cocycle needs Conrad's Modularity lifting seminar, Lecture 6. The paper sketches the proof.

items.name: Proposition 3.34: completions of Λ ⊗_O A^gen are framed deformation rings
items.statement: Let x be a closed point of X^gen (so κ(x) is finite over k, finite over L, or a local field of characteristic p), ρ_x the associated representation, and 𝔮 the kernel of Λ ⊗_O A^gen → κ(x), λ ⊗ a ↦ λ̄ā. Then the completion of (Λ ⊗_O A^gen)_𝔮 at its maximal ideal is naturally isomorphic to R^□_{ρ_x}.

items.name: Lemma 3.35: completion after base change to κ(𝔭) in characteristic p
items.statement: Let R be a complete local Noetherian k-algebra with residue field k, A a finitely generated R-algebra, 𝔭 ∈ Spec A with image in P_1R, and 𝔮 the kernel of B := κ(𝔭) ⊗_k A → κ(𝔭), x ⊗ a ↦ x(a + 𝔭). Then B̂_𝔮 ≅ Â_𝔭⟦T⟧; in particular A_𝔭 is regular (resp. a complete intersection) if and only if B̂_𝔮 is.

items.name: Lemma 3.36: completion after base change to an O-Cohen ring
items.statement: Let R be a complete local Noetherian O-algebra with residue field k, A a finitely generated R-algebra, 𝔭 ∈ Spec A with κ(𝔭) a local field of characteristic p, Λ an O-Cohen ring of κ(𝔭), and 𝔮 the kernel of B := Λ ⊗_O A → κ(𝔭), λ ⊗ a ↦ λ̄(a + 𝔭). Then B̂_𝔮 ≅ Â_𝔭⟦T⟧; in particular A_𝔭 is regular (resp. a complete intersection) if and only if B̂_𝔮 is.

items.name: Lemma 3.37: completion after base change when κ(𝔭) is finite over k or L
items.statement: Let R be a complete local Noetherian O-algebra with residue field k, A a finitely generated R-algebra, 𝔭 ∈ Spec A with κ(𝔭) a finite extension of L or of k, Λ as in item 046 for κ(𝔭), and 𝔮 the kernel of B := Λ ⊗_O A → κ(𝔭). Then B̂_𝔮 ≅ Â_𝔭.

items.name: Regularity and complete intersection are detected on completions
items.statement: A Noetherian local ring is regular (resp. a complete intersection) if and only if its completion is; if B → C is a local flat map with regular closed fibre, as for B → B⟦T⟧, then B is regular (resp. a complete intersection) if and only if C is.
items.locator: Used in Lemmas 3.35–3.37, pp. 24–25, and Remark 3.43, p. 26 (arXiv v2 pp. 27–30)
items.note: Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 4D plans 'preservation and reflection of regularity and dimension under completion of noetherian local rings'; the complete-intersection half belongs with R03.3's complete-intersection theory. Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean:51) without the completion theorem.

items.name: Corollary 3.38 (with Corollary 1.10): R^□_{ρ_x} is a flat complete intersection of relative dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p]
items.statement: Let x be a closed point of Y (the preimage of 𝔪_{R^ps} in X^gen) or of X^gen ∖ Y. Then (1) R^□_{ρ_x} is a flat Λ-algebra of relative dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p] and a complete intersection; (2) if char κ(x) = p, R^□_{ρ_x}/ϖ is a complete intersection of dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p].
items.locator: Corollary 3.38, p. 25 (arXiv v2 p. 28); Corollary 1.10, p. 5

items.name: Corollary 3.39: completed local rings of X^gen are framed deformation rings
items.statement: Let x be a closed point of Y or of X^gen ∖ Y. If κ(x) is a finite extension of k or L then Ô_{X^gen,x} ≅ R^□_{ρ_x}; if κ(x) is a local field of characteristic p then R^□_{ρ_x} ≅ Ô_{X^gen,x}⟦T⟧.

items.name: Corollary 3.40 (with Corollary 1.11): A^gen and A^gen/ϖ are equidimensional local complete intersections
items.statement: (1) A^gen is O-torsion free, equidimensional of dimension 1 + d² + d²[F:Q_p], and a local complete intersection; (2) A^gen/ϖ is equidimensional of dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p] and a local complete intersection.
items.locator: Corollary 3.40, p. 26 (arXiv v2 p. 29); Corollary 1.11, p. 5

items.name: Proposition 3.41: completions of R^□_ρ̄ at points of P_1 are framed deformation rings
items.statement: Let k' be a finite extension of k, R^□_ρ̄ the framed deformation ring of ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k'), x ∈ P_1R^□_ρ̄, ρ_x: G_F → GL_d(κ(x)) the specialisation of the universal framed deformation, Λ as in item 046 for κ(x), and 𝔮 the kernel of Λ ⊗_O R^□_ρ̄ → κ(x), λ ⊗ a ↦ λ̄ā. Then the completion of (Λ ⊗_O R^□_ρ̄)_𝔮 at its maximal ideal is naturally isomorphic to R^□_{ρ_x}.
items.note: Closely modelled on Kisin, Overconvergent modular forms and the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture, Proposition 9.5, and Böckle–Juschka Theorem 3.3.1 for versal rings.

items.name: Corollary 3.42 (with Remark 3.43): the same completion reached from X^gen and from R^□_{ρ_z}
items.statement: For a closed point x of X^gen, a closed point z of X^gen above 𝔪_{R^ps} and x' ∈ Spec R^□_{ρ_z} over x, there are isomorphisms of local Λ-algebras between R^□_{ρ_x}, R^□_{ρ_{x'}} and the completion of (Λ ⊗_O R^□_{ρ_z})_𝔮 at its maximal ideal, with 𝔮 as in Proposition 3.41 for x': R^□_{ρ_z} → O_{κ(x)}. Hence X^gen is regular (resp. a local complete intersection) at all closed points iff R^□_{ρ_z} is for all closed z above 𝔪_{R^ps}.
items.locator: Corollary 3.42, p. 26 (arXiv v2 p. 30); Remark 3.43, p. 26

items.name: Corollary 3.44: the conclusion of Corollary 3.38 for representations over local fields
items.statement: Let ρ: G_F → GL_d(κ) be continuous with κ a local field. Then R^□_ρ is a flat Λ-algebra of relative dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p] and a complete intersection, and if char κ = p then R^□_ρ/ϖ is a complete intersection of dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p].

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (Corollaries 3.38 and 3.45): R^□_ρ̄ is a local complete intersection, O-flat, of relative dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p]; every ρ̄ lifts to characteristic zero
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. Then R^□_ρ̄ is a local complete intersection, flat over O and of relative dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p], and R^□_ρ̄/ϖ is a complete intersection of dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p]. In particular R^□_ρ̄[1/p] ≠ 0, so every continuous ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) has a lift to characteristic zero.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p. 2 (arXiv v2 p. 2); Corollary 3.45, p. 27 (arXiv v2 p. 30)
items.note: The first main theorem. R^□_ρ̄ is the completion of A^gen at the closed point of ρ̄ (Proposition 3.34), so Corollary 3.38 applies.

items.name: Definition 3.46: the maximally reducible semisimple locus X^mrs
items.statement: Take 𝒫 = 𝒫_max with an ordering Σ, so that R^ps_Σ ≅ R_{ρ̄_1} ⊗̂_O ⋯ ⊗̂_O R_{ρ̄_m} with R_{ρ̄_i} the universal deformation ring of an absolutely irreducible ρ̄_i: G_F → GL_{d_i}(k) with pseudo-character D̄_i. Conjugating diag(ρ^univ_1, …, ρ^univ_m) by the universal matrix of GL_d gives GL_d ×_O X^ps_Σ → X^gen, which descends to η_Σ: GL_d/Z_L ×_O X^ps_Σ → X^gen (L the block Levi). X^mrs ⊂ X^gen is the scheme-theoretic image of η_Σ.
items.locator: Definition 3.46, p. 28 (arXiv v2 p. 31); construction on pp. 27–28

items.name: Lemma 3.47: semisimple points over X^ps_{𝒫_max} lie in X^mrs and are dense in it
items.statement: Let x ∈ X^gen with image y in X^ps. If y ∈ X^ps_{𝒫_max} and ρ_x is semisimple then x ∈ X^mrs; such points are dense in X^mrs.

items.name: Proposition 3.48 and Corollary 3.49: dimension of the maximally reducible semisimple locus
items.statement: dim X^mrs ≤ 1 + d² + [F:Q_p] Σ_{i=1}^m d_i², and dim X̄^mrs = dim X^mrs − 1 ≤ d² + [F:Q_p] Σ_{i=1}^m d_i².
items.locator: Proposition 3.48, p. 28 (arXiv v2 p. 31); Corollary 3.49, p. 29 (arXiv v2 p. 32); Remark 3.50
items.note: Used only for d = 2, F = Q_2 and D̄ reducible (Case 3 of Proposition 4.13). Item 060 is corrected for source issue E3 (ρ̄_i valued in GL_d(k)). Source issue E4 (X̄^ps for X^ps in its proof) does not affect the statement.

items.name: Special points (Böckle–Juschka), the loci U^spcl, V^spcl, Z^spcl, U^nspcl, and the Kummer loci U^Kirr, U^Kred, V^Kirr, Z^Kred
items.statement: U_{𝒫_min} is open in X̄^ps, and its closed points are the 𝔭 ∈ P_1(R^ps/ϖ) at which the specialised pseudo-character is absolutely irreducible. A point y ∈ U_{𝒫_min} is special if either ζ_p ∉ F and D_y = D_y(1), or ζ_p ∈ F and the restriction of D_y to G_{F'} is reducible for some degree-p Galois extension F'/F (Böckle–Juschka, Definition 5.1.2); by Böckle–Juschka Lemma 5.1.3 there is a closed subscheme U^spcl ⊂ U_{𝒫_min} whose closed points are the closed special points. V^spcl is its preimage in X̄^gen and Z^spcl the closure; U^nspcl = U_{𝒫_min} ∖ U^spcl. With U^Kirr the Kummer-irreducible locus (item 123), U^Kred is its complement in U_{𝒫_min}, V^Kred, V^Kirr the preimages and Z^Kred the closure of V^Kred; V^spcl ⊆ V^Kred and V^Kirr ⊆ V^nspcl, with equality if ζ_p ∈ F.

items.name: Proposition 3.51: V_{𝒫_min} is dense in X̄^gen
items.statement: V_{𝒫_min} is dense in X̄^gen; in particular dim Z_{𝒫_min} = d² + d²[F:Q_p].

items.name: Lemma 3.52: codimension of the special and Kummer-reducible loci in X̄^gen
items.statement: dim X̄^gen − dim Z^spcl ≥ ½[F:Q_p]d², and dim X̄^gen − dim Z^Kred ≥ [F:Q_p]d.

items.name: Proposition 3.53: the Kummer-irreducible locus V^Kirr is dense in X̄^gen, with codimension bounds for its complement
items.statement: V^Kirr is Zariski dense in X̄^gen, and (1) if d = 2 then dim X̄^gen − dim(X̄^gen ∖ V^Kirr) ≥ [F:Q_p]; (2) if d > 2 then dim X̄^gen − dim(X̄^gen ∖ V^Kirr) ≥ 1 + [F:Q_p]; (3) if d > 1 and D̄ is absolutely irreducible (m = 1) then dim X̄^gen − dim(X̄^gen ∖ V^Kirr) ≥ d[F:Q_p].

items.name: Lemma 3.54: preimages of dense opens under flat maps are dense
items.statement: Let A → B be a flat ring homomorphism, U an open subscheme of Spec A and V its preimage in Spec B. If U is dense in Spec A then V is dense in Spec B.
items.note: Follows from going-down for flat maps, which Mathlib has (Algebra.HasGoingDown.of_flat, Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/GoingDown.lean:154); the density statement itself is not in either library.

items.name: Proposition 3.55 and Remark 3.56 (with Proposition 1.12(2)): the Kummer-irreducible locus is dense in Spec R^□_ρ̄/ϖ
items.statement: Let (Spec R^□_ρ̄/ϖ)^Kirr be the preimage of V^Kirr in Spec R^□_ρ̄/ϖ. It is open and dense in Spec R^□_ρ̄/ϖ; its closed points are the x ∈ P_1(R^□_ρ̄/ϖ) over P_1(R^ps/ϖ) for which ρ_x: G_F → GL_d(κ(x)) stays absolutely irreducible on G_{F'} for every degree-p Galois extension F' of F(ζ_p), and H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ_x) = 0 at such x. In particular the Kummer-irreducible points x with κ(x) a local field are dense in Spec R^□_ρ̄/ϖ.
items.locator: Proposition 3.55, p. 30 (arXiv v2 p. 34); Remark 3.56, p. 30; Proposition 1.12(2), p. 6

items.name: The strata X^ps_𝒫 and X^gen_𝒫 of the generic fibre
items.statement: For each partition 𝒫, X^ps_𝒫 is the scheme-theoretic image of X^ps_Σ = Spec R^ps_Σ in X^ps under the product map, and X^gen_𝒫 is its preimage in X^gen. (It is not known that X̄^ps_𝒫 is the special fibre of X^ps_𝒫.)
items.note: Corrected for source issue E5, which prints the image of X^ps inside X^ps_Σ.

items.name: Lemma 3.57: dim X^gen_𝒫[1/p] ≤ dim X̄^gen_𝒫
items.statement: dim X^gen_𝒫[1/p] ≤ dim X̄^gen_𝒫.

items.name: Proposition 3.58: the absolutely irreducible locus V^irr is open and dense in X^gen[1/p]
items.statement: Let V^irr := X^gen[1/p] ∖ ⋃_{𝒫_min<𝒫} X^gen_𝒫[1/p]. Then V^irr is open and dense in X^gen[1/p], and (1) if d = 2 then dim X^gen[1/p] − dim(X^gen[1/p] ∖ V^irr) ≥ [F:Q_p]; (2) if d > 2 this codimension is ≥ 1 + [F:Q_p]; (3) if d > 1 and D̄ is absolutely irreducible then X^gen[1/p] = V^irr.

items.name: Corollary 3.59 and Remark 3.60 (with Proposition 1.12(1)): absolutely irreducible points are dense in Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p]
items.statement: The preimage (Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p])^irr of V^irr is open and dense in Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p]; its closed points are the maximal ideals 𝔭 of R^□_ρ̄[1/p] with ρ_𝔭: G_F → GL_d(κ(𝔭)) absolutely irreducible. So the absolutely irreducible points x with κ(x) finite over L are dense in Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p].
items.locator: Corollary 3.59, p. 31 (arXiv v2 p. 35); Remark 3.60, p. 31; Proposition 1.12(1), p. 6

items.name: Corollary 3.61: the characteristic-zero lift may be chosen absolutely irreducible
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. Then ρ̄ has an absolutely irreducible lift to characteristic zero.
items.locator: Corollary 3.61, p. 32 (arXiv v2 p. 35); Proposition 1.12, p. 6

items.name: Corollary 3.62: dense sets of maximal ideals stay dense after intersecting with the irreducible locus
items.statement: If Σ ⊂ MaxSpec R^□_ρ̄[1/p] is dense in Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p], then Σ^irr := Σ ∩ (Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p])^irr is also dense.

items.name: Lemma 4.1: the universal deformation ring of a character
items.statement: Let ψ̄: G_F → k^× be a continuous character, R_ψ̄ its universal deformation ring and μ := μ_{p^∞}(F) (a finite cyclic p-group). Local class field theory gives μ → F^× → G_F^ab → GL_1(R_ψ̄), hence O[μ] → R_ψ̄, and R_ψ̄ ≅ O[μ]⟦y_1, …, y_{[F:Q_p]+1}⟧. So the irreducible components of Spec R_ψ̄ are indexed by the characters χ: μ → O^×, and R_ψ̄ ⊗_{O[μ],χ} O is formally smooth over O.
items.locator: Lemma 4.1, p. 32 (arXiv v2 p. 36); and the paragraph after it
items.note: The proof uses that the pro-p completion of G_F^ab is μ × Z_p^{[F:Q_p]+1} (local class field theory: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 7 plans the absolute local Artin map) and Gouvêa's Proposition 3.13.

items.name: Local class field theory: the pro-p completion of G_F^ab and characters of F^×
items.statement: The Artin map Art_F: F^× → G_F^ab identifies continuous characters G_F → O^× with continuous characters F^× → O^×; the pro-p completion of G_F^ab is isomorphic to μ_{p^∞}(F) × Z_p^{[F:Q_p]+1}, and the maximal torsion-free quotient of G_F^ab is Ẑ × Z_p^{[F:Q_p]}.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 4.1, p. 32, and Lemmas 6.4–6.5, p. 47 (arXiv v2 pp. 36, 53)
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 7 plans the absolute local Artin map K^× → G_K^ab with dense image and its normalisations.

items.name: The component rings R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ (fixing the determinant on Art_F(μ) only), A^{gen,χ}, R^{ps,χ}, and the decomposition of R^□_ρ̄[1/p]
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. Via R_{det ρ̄} → R^□_ρ̄ and Lemma 4.1, R^□_ρ̄ is an O[μ]-algebra; since O[μ][1/p] is semisimple with maximal ideals indexed by characters χ: μ → O^×, R^□_ρ̄[1/p] ≅ ∏_χ R^{□,χ}_ρ̄[1/p] with R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ := R^□_ρ̄ ⊗_{O[μ],χ} O. R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ represents D^{□,χ}_ρ̄(A) = {ρ_A ∈ D^□_ρ̄(A) : det ρ_A(Art_F(x)) = χ(x) for all x ∈ μ}; it is not a fixed-determinant ring (Warning 4.2). Similarly A^{gen,χ} := A^gen ⊗_{O[μ],χ} O, X^{gen,χ} = Spec A^{gen,χ}, R^{ps,χ} := R^ps ⊗_{O[μ],χ} O, and R^{□,χ}_ρ for ρ over κ as in item 046.
items.locator: §4, (25), p. 33 (arXiv v2 p. 36); Warning 4.2, p. 33; before Corollary 4.27, p. 41

items.name: Proposition 4.3: presentation of R^□_ρ̄ over R_{det ρ̄} by a regular sequence
items.statement: There is an isomorphism R_{det ρ̄}⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧/(f_1, …, f_t) ≅ R^□_ρ̄ with r = dim_k Z^1(G_F, ad^0 ρ̄) and t = dim_k H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ̄), such that f_1, …, f_t is a regular sequence in R_{det ρ̄}⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧; moreover r − t = (d² − 1)([F:Q_p] + 1).
items.locator: Proposition 4.3, p. 33 (arXiv v2 p. 37); Remark 4.4, p. 35
items.note: Obstruction theory relative to the determinant (a continuous set-theoretic section exists by Ribes–Zalesskii Proposition 2.2.2), then regularity of the sequence from Theorem 1.1 by a dimension count.

items.name: Corollary 4.5: R^{□,χ}_{ρ_x} is an O-torsion free complete intersection of dimension 1 + d² + d²[F:Q_p]
items.statement: For each character χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^× and each closed point x ∈ X^gen above 𝔪_{R^ps}: (1) R^{□,χ}_{ρ_x} is O-torsion free of dimension 1 + d² + d²[F:Q_p] and a complete intersection; (2) R^{□,χ}_{ρ_x}/ϖ is a complete intersection of dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p].
items.locator: Corollary 4.5, p. 35 (arXiv v2 p. 38); Remark 4.7, p. 36

items.name: Corollary 4.6: A^{gen,χ} and A^{gen,χ}/ϖ are equidimensional local complete intersections
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^×: (1) A^{gen,χ} is O-torsion free, equidimensional of dimension 1 + d² + d²[F:Q_p], and a local complete intersection; (2) A^{gen,χ}/ϖ is equidimensional of dimension d² + d²[F:Q_p] and a local complete intersection.

items.name: Lemma 4.8: vanishing of H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ) gives formal smoothness of R^{□,χ}_ρ
items.statement: Let ρ: G_F → GL_d(κ) be continuous, κ a finite extension of k, a local field of characteristic p, or a finite extension of L. If H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ) = 0 then for every χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^× the ring R^{□,χ}_ρ is formally smooth over Λ.
items.note: Adapts Böckle–Juschka Lemma 3.4.2 (unframed, Artinian κ-algebras): R_{det ρ} → R^□_ρ is formally smooth when H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ) = 0.

items.name: Proposition 4.9: the absolutely irreducible non-special locus of X̄^{gen,χ} is regular
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^×, the absolutely irreducible non-special locus V^nspcl ∩ X̄^{gen,χ} is regular.
items.note: Uses Böckle–Juschka Lemma 5.1.1: at non-special x, H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ_x) = 0 (ζ_p ∈ F) or H^2(G_F, ad ρ_x) = 0 (ζ_p ∉ F).

items.name: Proposition 4.10: the absolutely irreducible locus of X^{gen,χ}[1/p] is regular
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^×, the absolutely irreducible locus in X^{gen,χ}[1/p] is regular.

items.name: Lemma 4.11: H^2 vanishing for d = 2, F = Q_p with residually non-cyclotomic reducible semisimplification
items.statement: Assume F = Q_p and d = 2, κ a finite extension of L or a finite or local field of characteristic p, with p > 2 if char κ = p. Let ρ: G_{Q_p} → GL_2(κ) have semisimplification ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 with ψ_1 ≠ ψ_2(1) and ψ_2 ≠ ψ_1(1). Then H^2(G_{Q_p}, ad ρ) = H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ) = 0; in particular R^{□,χ}_ρ is formally smooth over Λ.

items.name: Lemma 4.12: H^2 vanishing for p = 2, F = Q_2, d = 2 non-split extensions of distinct characters
items.statement: Assume p = 2, F = Q_2, d = 2, κ a finite or local field of characteristic 2, and ρ: G_{Q_2} → GL_2(κ) a non-split extension of distinct characters. Then H^2(G_{Q_2}, ad^0 ρ) = 0; in particular R^{□,χ}_ρ is formally smooth over Λ.

items.name: Proposition 4.13: X̄^{gen,χ} is regular in codimension one
items.statement: There is an open subscheme V^{0,χ} ⊂ X̄^{gen,χ} such that (1) H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ_x) = 0 for all closed points x ∈ V^{0,χ}; (2) dim X̄^{gen,χ} − dim(X̄^{gen,χ} ∖ V^{0,χ}) ≥ 2. In particular X̄^{gen,χ} is regular in codimension 1.
items.note: Three cases: if d > 2, F ≠ Q_p or D̄ is irreducible, take V^{0,χ} = V^Kirr ∩ X̄^{gen,χ} (Proposition 3.53, Lemma A.2); if d = 2, F = Q_p, p > 2 and D̄ is reducible, remove Y, Z^{12}_{𝒫_max}, Z^{21}_{𝒫_max} and Z^Kred and use Lemma 4.11; if d = 2, F = Q_2 and D̄ is reducible, use Lemma 4.12 and also remove the reducible semisimple locus (dimension ≤ 6 < 8, Corollary 3.49).

items.name: Serre's criterion for normality, with Cohen–Macaulayness of complete intersections
items.statement: A Noetherian ring is normal if and only if it satisfies (R1) and (S2); a complete intersection (in particular a local complete intersection scheme) is Cohen–Macaulay and so satisfies (S_n) for all n; local complete intersection is inherited by localisations and detected on completions (Stacks 09Q3–09Q5).
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 4.14, p. 38, Proposition 4.17, p. 39, Theorem 5.6, p. 44 (arXiv v2 pp. 43–44, 49); Corollary 3.40

items.name: Excellence: finitely generated algebras over complete local Noetherian rings are excellent; an excellent local ring is normal iff its completion is
items.statement: A finitely generated algebra over a complete local Noetherian ring is excellent, so are its localisations, and an excellent local ring is reduced (resp. normal) if and only if its completion is (Matsumura, Commutative ring theory, Theorem 32.2(i)); the regular locus of such an algebra is open.
items.locator: Proofs of Corollary 4.15, p. 38, and Corollary 5.8, p. 45 (arXiv v2 pp. 43, 50)
items.note: R03.3 asks for catenarity and excellence as explicit hypotheses; its audit records no catenary or excellent predicate in either library. Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 4D plans openness of the regular locus over an excellent base.

items.name: Proposition 4.14: X̄^{gen,χ} is normal
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^×, X̄^{gen,χ} is normal.

items.name: Corollary 4.15 (part of Theorem 1.2): R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ is a normal domain
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^× and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k), R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ is a normal integral domain.
items.note: Normal and complete local, hence a domain. The proof's reference 'Proposition 3.37' means Lemma 3.37 (source issue E8).

items.name: Lemma 4.16: loci where H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ_x) ≠ 0 away from the closed fibre have codimension at least 2 in R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ
items.statement: Let Ŷ be the preimage of 𝔪_{R^ps} in Spec R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ and W a closed subscheme of Spec R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ with H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ_x) ≠ 0 for all closed points x ∈ W ∖ Ŷ. Then dim R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ − dim W ≥ 2.

items.name: Proposition 4.17: X^{gen,χ}[1/p] is normal
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^×, X^{gen,χ}[1/p] is normal.

items.name: Corollary 4.18: X^{gen,χ} is normal
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^×, X^{gen,χ} is normal.

items.name: Corollary 4.19 (part of Theorem 1.2): R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ is a normal domain
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^× and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k), R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ is a normal integral domain.

items.name: Lemma 4.20: H^2-nonvanishing loci have codimension at least 2 in the generic fibre
items.statement: Let W be a closed subscheme of Spec R^{□,χ}_ρ̄[1/p] with H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ_x) ≠ 0 for all closed points x ∈ W. Then dim R^{□,χ}_ρ̄[1/p] − dim W ≥ 2.

items.name: Corollary 4.21 (Theorem 1.2): R_{det ρ̄} → R^□_ρ̄ induces a bijection on irreducible components, and on π_0 of generic fibres
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. The map R_{det ρ̄} → R^□_ρ̄ induces a bijection between the sets of irreducible components, and a bijection π_0(Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p]) → π_0(Spec R_{det ρ̄}[1/p]); both are indexed by the characters χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^× (L large enough), the component for χ being Spec R^{□,χ}_ρ̄, which is a normal domain and a complete intersection, as is R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ.
items.locator: Corollary 4.21, p. 40 (arXiv v2 p. 44); Theorem 1.2 and (1), p. 2
items.note: Answers Böckle–Juschka's question in the (p, p)-case paper (J. Algebra 444 (2015), Question 1.10).

items.name: Corollary 4.22 (with Corollary 1.3): R^□_ρ̄ is reduced and R^□_ρ̄[1/p] is normal
items.statement: R^□_ρ̄[1/p] is normal and R^□_ρ̄ is reduced.
items.locator: Corollary 4.22, p. 40 (arXiv v2 p. 45); Corollary 1.3, p. 2

items.name: Grothendieck's parafactoriality theorem
items.statement: A local complete intersection ring that is regular in codimension ≤ 3 (its localisations at primes of height ≤ 3 are regular) is factorial (Grothendieck, SGA 2 XI; Call–Lyubeznik's short proof).
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 4.23, p. 40 (arXiv v2 p. 45)
items.note: Mathlib has UniqueFactorizationMonoid (Mathlib/RingTheory/UniqueFactorizationDomain/Defs.lean:133) but not this theorem, nor Auslander–Buchsbaum (regular local rings are factorial).

items.name: Corollary 4.23: R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ are factorial when [F:Q_p] is large enough
items.statement: If either d = 2 and [F:Q_p] ≥ 4, or d ≥ 3 and [F:Q_p] ≥ 3, then for every χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^× and ρ̄, the rings R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ are regular in codimension 3, hence factorial.
items.locator: Corollary 4.23, p. 40 (arXiv v2 p. 45); Remark 4.24, p. 40
items.note: Remark 4.24: for F = Q_p, p ≥ 5 and ρ̄ = (1 ∗; 0 ω) non-split, R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ ≅ O⟦x_1, …, x_9⟧/(x_1x_2 − x_3x_4) (Paškūnas, The image of Colmez's Montreal functor, Corollary B.5), which is not factorial; some hypothesis is needed.

items.name: Two-dimensional computations at F = Q_2 and F = Q_3
items.statement: (1) If p = 2, F = Q_2, d = 2 and ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄(1) is absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ is formally smooth over O[μ] (Chenevier, Sur la variété des caractères p-adique du groupe de Galois absolu de Q_p, Proposition 4.5). (2) If p = 3, F = Q_3, d = 2 and ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄(1) is absolutely irreducible, R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ is formally smooth over O⟦b, c, d⟧/(r) with r = (1 + d)^6(1 + bcu) − (1 + bcv) for units u, v ∈ O⟦b, c⟧ (Böckle, Deformation rings for some mod 3 Galois representations of the absolute Galois group of Q_3, Theorem 5.1).
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 4.25, p. 41 (arXiv v2 p. 46)
items.note: Imported from Chenevier's unpublished note (2010) and Böckle (Astérisque 330, 2010). LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.5 plans dyadic calculations for KW II and Kisin's 2-adic Barsotti–Tate theorem, not these unrestricted rings.

items.name: Corollary 4.25 (Theorem 1.4): factoriality for absolutely irreducible ρ̄, with the exception d = 2, F = Q_3, ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄(1)
items.statement: If ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible then R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ are factorial, except in the case d = 2, F = Q_3 and ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄(1), where R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ are not factorial.
items.locator: Corollary 4.25, p. 40 (arXiv v2 p. 45); Theorem 1.4, p. 2
items.note: In the exceptional case the height-one prime (b, d) of Böckle's presentation is not principal (Stacks 0AFT).

items.name: Proposition 4.26: A^{gen,χ} and A^{gen,χ}/ϖ are domains
items.statement: For each χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^×, the rings A^{gen,χ} and A^{gen,χ}/ϖ are integral domains.

items.name: Paškūnas–Tung: invariants of the generic fibre, and normality of the rigid pseudodeformation space
items.statement: If A^gen[1/p] is normal (Corollary 4.22 gives this through X^gen), then R^ps[1/p] = (A^gen[1/p])^{GL_d} and R^ps[1/p] and the rigid space (Spf R^ps)^rig are normal (Paškūnas–Tung, Finiteness properties of the category of mod p representations of GL_2(Q_p), Theorem A.1 and Corollary A.10).
items.locator: Proofs of Corollary 4.27, p. 41, and Corollary 5.10, p. 45 (arXiv v2 pp. 46, 50)
items.note: Imported; a prerequisite paper. The appendix of Paškūnas–Tung is written for general d.

items.name: Corollary 4.27: normality of R^ps[1/p] and R^{ps,χ}[1/p], and components of the generic pseudodeformation space
items.statement: R^ps[1/p], R^{ps,χ}[1/p] and the rigid spaces (Spf R^ps)^rig, (Spf R^{ps,χ})^rig are normal; R^{ps,χ}[1/p] is an integral domain, so R_{det ρ̄}[1/p] → R^ps[1/p] induces a bijection between the sets of irreducible components.

items.name: Corollary 4.28: the image of R^ps in A^gen is its maximal reduced and maximal O-torsion free quotient
items.statement: The image of R^ps in A^gen is the maximal O-torsion free quotient of R^ps and also its maximal reduced quotient; in particular R_{det D̄} → R^ps → R^ps[1/p] induces a bijection between the sets of irreducible components. If D̄ is multiplicity free, R^ps is reduced and O-torsion free.

items.name: Corollary 4.29: images of R^{ps,χ} and R^{ps,χ}/ϖ in A^{gen,χ}
items.statement: The image of R^{ps,χ}/ϖ in A^{gen,χ}/ϖ is the maximal reduced quotient of R^{ps,χ}/ϖ; the image of R^{ps,χ} in A^{gen,χ} is the maximal reduced quotient of R^{ps,χ} and its maximal O-torsion free quotient. If D̄ is multiplicity free, R^{ps,χ}/ϖ and R^{ps,χ} are integral domains.

items.name: Lemma 4.30: (S1) for R^{ps,χ}/ϖ would make R^{ps,χ}/ϖ and R^{ps,χ} domains
items.statement: If R^{ps,χ}/ϖ satisfies Serre's condition (S1), then R^{ps,χ}/ϖ and R^{ps,χ} are integral domains.
items.locator: Lemma 4.30, p. 42 (arXiv v2 p. 47); Remark 4.31, p. 42
items.note: Remark 4.31 expects R^{ps,χ} and R^{ps,χ}/ϖ always to be domains; a presentation like (21) for R^ps is missing. The proof's 'Lemma 4.29' is Corollary 4.29 and its 'universal deformation ring of R_{ρ_x}' means of ρ_x (source issues E8, E6).

items.name: The fixed-determinant framed ring R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. For a character ψ: G_F → O^× lifting det ρ̄, R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ := R^□_ρ̄ ⊗_{R_{det ρ̄},ψ} O, representing framed deformations with determinant ψ; if χ = ψ ∘ Art_F on μ, R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ is a quotient of R^{□,χ}_ρ̄. X^{□,χ}, X^{□,ψ} are their spectra and X̄^{□,χ}, X̄^{□,ψ} their special fibres.
items.note: R08.1 plans 'the effect of fixing the determinant'.

items.name: The functor 𝒳 of characters trivial on Art_F(μ), its ring O(𝒳) ≅ O⟦y_1, …, y_{[F:Q_p]+1}⟧, and the power maps φ_e
items.statement: 𝒳: 𝔄_O → Sets sends (A, 𝔪_A) to the group of continuous characters θ: G_F → 1 + 𝔪_A whose restriction to μ under the Artin map is trivial; by Lemma 4.1 it is pro-represented by O(𝒳) ≅ R_1 ⊗_{O[μ]} O ≅ O⟦y_1, …, y_{[F:Q_p]+1}⟧. For e ∈ N, φ_e: 𝒳 → 𝒳 is θ ↦ θ^e, also written for the maps of O(𝒳) and Spec O(𝒳). ρ ↦ (det ρ)ψ^{−1} makes R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ an O(𝒳)-algebra.

items.name: Proposition 5.1: twisting identifies D^{□,χ} ×_{𝒳,φ_d} 𝒳 with D^{□,ψ} × 𝒳
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism of functors D^{□,χ}_ρ̄ ×_{𝒳,φ_d} 𝒳 ≅ D^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ × 𝒳, (ρ, θ) ↦ (ρ ⊗ θ^{−1}, θ).

items.name: Corollary 5.2: R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ ⊗_{O(𝒳),φ_d} O(𝒳) ≅ R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ ⊗̂_O O(𝒳)
items.statement: Proposition 5.1 induces a natural isomorphism R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ ⊗_{O(𝒳),φ_d} O(𝒳) ≅ R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ ⊗̂_O O(𝒳).

items.name: Lemma 5.3: φ_d is finite flat, étale after inverting p, and a universal homeomorphism on special fibres
items.statement: The map φ_d: O(𝒳) → O(𝒳) is finite and flat and becomes étale after inverting p; it induces a universal homeomorphism on the special fibres.

items.name: Corollary 5.4: R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ is an O-flat local complete intersection of relative dimension (d² − 1)([F:Q_p] + 1)
items.statement: (1) R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ is a local complete intersection, flat over O, of relative dimension (d² − 1)([F:Q_p] + 1); (2) R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄/ϖ is a local complete intersection of dimension (d² − 1)([F:Q_p] + 1).

items.name: Lemma 5.5: formal smoothness of R^{□,ψ}_ρ when H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ) = 0
items.statement: Let ρ: G_F → GL_d(κ) with det ρ = ψ, κ a finite or local field of characteristic p or a finite extension of L. If H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ) = 0 then R^{□,ψ}_ρ is formally smooth over Λ.

items.name: Theorem 5.6 (with Theorem 1.5): R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄/ϖ are normal domains and complete intersections
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. For a character ψ lifting det ρ̄, R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄/ϖ are normal integral domains and complete intersections, of dimensions dim R^□_ρ̄ − dim R_{det ρ̄} + 1 and dim R^□_ρ̄ − dim R_{det ρ̄}; R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄ is O-flat.
items.locator: Theorem 5.6, p. 44 (arXiv v2 p. 49); Theorem 1.5, p. 3
items.note: The Kummer-irreducible locus of the appendix is what makes the argument work when ζ_p ∉ F.

items.name: Corollary 5.7: density of the irreducible loci with fixed determinant
items.statement: The absolutely irreducible locus is dense in Spec R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄[1/p], and the Kummer-irreducible locus is dense in Spec R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄/ϖ.

items.name: Corollary 5.8: A^{gen,ψ} and A^{gen,ψ}/ϖ are equidimensional, normal local complete intersections
items.statement: (1) A^{gen,ψ} is O-flat, equidimensional of dimension 1 + (d² − 1)([F:Q_p] + 1), normal and a local complete intersection; (2) A^{gen,ψ}/ϖ is equidimensional of dimension (d² − 1)([F:Q_p] + 1), normal and a local complete intersection.

items.name: Corollary 5.9: A^{gen,ψ} and A^{gen,ψ}/ϖ are domains
items.statement: The rings A^{gen,ψ} and A^{gen,ψ}/ϖ are integral domains.

items.name: Corollary 5.10: normality of R^{ps,ψ}[1/p]
items.statement: The ring R^{ps,ψ}[1/p] and the rigid space (Spf R^{ps,ψ})^rig are normal, and R^{ps,ψ}[1/p] is an integral domain.

items.name: Corollary 5.11: the maximal reduced quotient of R^{ps,ψ}
items.statement: The maximal reduced quotient of R^{ps,ψ} equals its maximal O-torsion free quotient and is an integral domain; if D̄ is multiplicity free, R^{ps,ψ} is an O-torsion free integral domain.

items.name: The fibrewise criterion for flatness
items.statement: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with A regular and B Cohen–Macaulay. If dim B = dim A + dim B/𝔪_A B then B is flat over A (Matsumura, Commutative ring theory, Theorem 23.1).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.12, p. 46 (arXiv v2 p. 51)
items.note: Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 4D plans miracle flatness only for finite morphisms of regular local schemes of equal dimension. The R03.3 audit records the dimension half (dim B = dim A + dim B/𝔪_A B for flat local maps) as partly in Mathlib.

items.name: Proposition 5.12 (Theorem 1.2): R_{det ρ̄} → R^□_ρ̄ is flat
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. The map R_{det ρ̄} → R^□_ρ̄, sending a deformation to its determinant, is flat.
items.locator: Proposition 5.12, p. 45 (arXiv v2 p. 50); Theorem 1.2, p. 2
items.note: With S = O⟦z, y_1, …, y_{1+[F:Q_p]}⟧ regular, R_{det ρ̄} ≅ S/((1 + z)^m − 1) and R^□_ρ̄ ≅ S'/((1 + z)^m − 1) for a complete intersection S' whose closed fibre R^{□,ψ}_ρ̄/ϖ has the right dimension (Corollary 5.4), so the fibrewise criterion applies.

items.name: Definition A.1: Kummer-irreducible points of Spec R^ps/ϖ
items.statement: For x ∈ X̄^ps let D_x = D^u ⊗_{R^ps} κ(x)‾ and ρ_x: G_F → GL_d(κ(x)‾) the semisimple representation with pseudo-character D_x. A point x ∈ P_1(R^ps/ϖ) is Kummer-irreducible if the restriction of D_x to G_{F'} is absolutely irreducible for every degree-p Galois extension F' of F(ζ_p), and Kummer-reducible otherwise. Equivalently ρ_x|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is non-special in the sense of Böckle–Juschka Definition 5.1.2; if ζ_p ∈ F the two notions agree.

items.name: Lemma A.2: H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ_x) = 0 at Kummer-irreducible points
items.statement: If x is Kummer-irreducible then H^2(G_F, ad^0 ρ_x) = 0.

items.name: Lemma A.3: restriction of pseudo-characters to an open subgroup is finite
items.statement: If E ⊂ F̄ is a finite extension of F, the morphism r: X^ps → X^ps_E induced by restricting pseudo-characters of G_F to G_E is finite.
items.note: The proof's reference 'Proposition 3.24' is Lemma 3.24 (source issue E8).

items.name: The loci U^irr, U^Kred, U^cred and U^spcl of X̄^ps, and Lemma A.4
items.statement: U^irr := U_{𝒫_min} is the absolutely irreducible locus of X̄^ps; U^Kred := U^irr ∩ ⋃_{F'} r^{−1}(X̄^ps_{F'} ∖ U^irr_{F'}), the union over the finitely many degree-p Galois extensions F' of F(ζ_p), is closed in U^irr; the cyclotomic-reducible locus U^cred := U^irr ∩ r^{−1}(X̄^ps_{F(ζ_p)} ∖ U^irr_{F(ζ_p)}) is closed and contained in U^Kred, equal to U^spcl if ζ_p ∉ F and empty otherwise. Lemma A.4: U^spcl ⊂ U^Kred, with equality if ζ_p ∈ F.
items.locator: Lemma A.4, p. 51 (arXiv v2 p. 57); definitions on p. 51

items.name: Lemma A.5: dimensions of locally closed subsets of U^irr and their closures
items.statement: Let T be a locally closed subset of U^irr, T̄ its closure in U^irr and Z its closure in X̄^ps. Then dim T = dim T̄ and dim Z = dim T + 1.
items.locator: Lemma A.5, p. 51 (arXiv v2 p. 57); Remark A.6 (Stacks 0DRT)

items.name: Lemma A.7: codimension of the cyclotomic-reducible locus
items.statement: dim U^irr = d²[F:Q_p] and dim U^irr − dim U^cred ≥ ½d²[F:Q_p], which is ≥ 2 when d ≥ 2.
items.locator: Lemma A.7, p. 51 (arXiv v2 p. 58); (36), p. 51
items.note: Corrected for source issue E9: the printed '≥ ½d²[F:Q_p] ≥ 2' fails numerically for d = 1 and [F:Q_p] ≤ 3 (where U^cred is empty).

items.name: Lemma A.8: codimension of the Kummer-reducible locus
items.statement: dim U^irr − dim U^Kred ≥ d[F:Q_p], which is ≥ 2 when d ≥ 2.
items.note: Uses Böckle–Juschka Lemma 5.1.1 and the proof of their Theorem 5.4.1 with [K':K] = p. Corrected for source issue E9 (printed '≥ d[F:Q_p] ≥ 2').

items.name: Proposition A.9: the Kummer-irreducible locus is open and dense in U^irr
items.statement: There is an open dense subscheme U^Kirr ⊂ U^irr such that x ∈ P_1(R^ps/ϖ) is Kummer-irreducible if and only if x is a closed point of U^Kirr; moreover dim U^irr − dim(U^irr ∖ U^Kirr) ≥ d[F:Q_p], which is ≥ 2 when d ≥ 2.
items.note: Corrected for source issue E9.

items.name: The sets Σ^cris, Σ_k, Σ^prnc_k and Σ^spcd_k of potentially semistable points of X^□ = Spec R^□_ρ̄
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. For x: R^□_ρ̄ → Q̄_p let ρ^□_x be the specialised universal framed deformation. Hodge–Tate weights k = (k_σ) with k_σ = (k_{σ,1} ≥ … ≥ k_{σ,d}) for σ: F → Q̄_p are regular if all inequalities are strict. Σ^cris is the set of x with ρ^□_x crystalline of regular Hodge–Tate weights; for fixed regular k, Σ_k is the set of x with ρ^□_x potentially semistable with HT(ρ^□_x) = k; Σ^prnc_k ⊂ Σ_k consists of the x for which LL(WD(ρ^□_x)), the irreducible smooth representation of GL_d(F) attached to the Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne representation by the classical local Langlands correspondence, is a principal series (equivalently ρ^□_x becomes crystalline over a finite abelian extension of F); Σ^spcd_k ⊂ Σ_k consists of the x for which WD(ρ^□_x) is irreducible and induced from a character of W_E, E/F unramified of degree d (so LL(WD(ρ^□_x)) is supercuspidal).
items.note: Hodge–Tate weights, D_cris and D_st are planned in PadicHodgeTheory R06.2, WD(ρ) in R06.3, and the classical local Langlands correspondence for GL_d with full Weil–Deligne parameters in EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6; the sets themselves are defined nowhere in the atlas.

items.name: Kisin: potentially semistable deformation rings are O-torsion free, reduced and equidimensional
items.statement: For a finite extension K/Q_p (a place ṽ above p of the auxiliary CM field), a continuous r̄: G_K → GL_d(k), a Hodge type ξ and an inertial type τ, the framed potentially semistable deformation ring R^{□,ξ,τ}_ṽ, whose Q̄_p-points are the potentially semistable lifts of type (ξ, τ), is O-torsion free, reduced and equidimensional (Kisin, Potentially semi-stable deformation rings, Theorem 3.3.8, as cited).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.3, p. 47 (arXiv v2 p. 52)

items.name: The patched module M_∞ of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin
items.statement: Assume p ∤ 2d and that ρ̄ has a potentially diagonalisable lift. Then there are a complete local Noetherian O-algebra R_∞ with residue field k and a linearly compact R_∞-module M_∞ with a continuous R_∞-linear action of G := GL_d(F), such that the action of R_∞[K], K := GL_d(O_F), extends uniquely to a continuous action of R_∞⟦K⟧ making M_∞ a finitely generated R_∞⟦K⟧-module. R_∞ is formally smooth over R^loc = R^□_ρ̄ ⊗̂_O R^□_{ṽ_1} ⊗̂_O ⊗̂_{v ∈ S_p ∖ 𝔭} R^{□,ξ,τ}_ṽ, with R^□_{ṽ_1} formally smooth over O (CEGGPS §§2.4–2.8, Lemma 2.5). The hypothesis on potentially diagonalisable lifts holds if ρ̄ is semisimple (CEGGPS Lemma 2.2) and always, by Emerton–Gee (item 135).
items.locator: §6, p. 46 (arXiv v2 p. 52); proof of Lemma 6.3, p. 47
items.note: Imported from Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin, Camb. J. Math. 4 (2016); a prerequisite paper. The atlas has patching for GL_2 over Q (CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.5) and abstract patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5, P8) but not this construction.

items.name: CEGGPS: central character, projectivity and crystalline support of M_∞
items.statement: Let ψ: G_F → O^× lift det ρ̄ with x: R_{det ρ̄} → O the corresponding map. (1) The centre Z ≅ F^× of G acts on M_∞ ⊗_{R_{det ρ̄},x} O through δ^{−1}, δ = (ε^{d(d−1)/2}ψ) ∘ Art_F (CEGGPS §4.22). (2) M_∞ ⊗_{R_{det ρ̄},x} O is non-zero and projective in the category of linearly compact O⟦K⟧-modules on which Z ∩ K acts by δ^{−1} (CEGGPS Corollary 4.26). (3) For an irreducible algebraic representation ξ of (Res^F_{Q_p} GL_d)_L, R^□_ρ̄/𝔞_ξ, with 𝔞_ξ the R^□_ρ̄-annihilator of M_∞(ξ), is a quotient of the crystalline deformation ring of ρ̄ with the Hodge–Tate weights of the highest weight of ξ and a union of its irreducible components (CEGGPS Lemma 4.18, §1.8; Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen Remark 5.14).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 6.6, p. 48, and Theorem 6.1, p. 49 (arXiv v2 pp. 54–55)
items.note: Imported from CEGGPS and Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen; prerequisite papers.

items.name: Emerton–Gee: existence of potentially diagonalisable (crystalline) lifts
items.statement: Every continuous ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) has a potentially diagonalisable lift, after enlarging k (Emerton–Gee, Moduli stacks of étale (φ, Γ)-modules and the existence of crystalline lifts, Theorem 1.2.2).
items.note: Imported; removes the potential diagonalisability hypothesis of CEGGPS. Its proof, through the Emerton–Gee stack, is not in the atlas; the Part II states it as a source-bound input (a prerequisite paper) rather than planning the stack.

items.name: Components of completed tensor products of O-flat reduced equidimensional complete local rings
items.statement: (1) If A and B are complete local Noetherian O-algebras with residue field k that are O-torsion free, reduced and equidimensional, so is A ⊗̂_O B (CEGGPS Corollary A.2; Hu–Paškūnas Lemma A.1). (2) After a finite extension of L, every minimal prime 𝔭 of such an A has A/𝔭 geometrically integral, i.e. (A/𝔭) ⊗_O O_{L'} is a domain for all finite L'/L (Hu–Paškūnas Lemma A.5). (3) If A/𝔭 and B/𝔭' are geometrically integral for all minimal primes, the minimal primes of A ⊗̂_O B are exactly the 𝔭(A ⊗̂ B) + 𝔭'(A ⊗̂ B) (Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 3.3(5)).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.3, p. 47 (arXiv v2 pp. 52–53)
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 plans completed tensor products over O and when they remain Noetherian and local, but not their minimal primes.

items.name: Lemma 6.3: R_∞ ≅ R^□_ρ̄ ⊗̂_O A and the irreducible components of Spec R_∞
items.statement: There is an isomorphism of R^□_ρ̄-algebras R_∞ ≅ R^□_ρ̄ ⊗̂_O A, where A is a complete local Noetherian O-algebra that is O-torsion free, reduced and equidimensional; thus R_∞ is a reduced, O-torsion free and flat R^□_ρ̄-algebra. After replacing L by a finite extension, the irreducible components of Spec R_∞ are the Spec(R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ ⊗̂_O A/𝔭) for characters χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^× and minimal primes 𝔭 of A, and distinct pairs (χ, 𝔭) give distinct components.

items.name: Lemma 6.4: d-th roots of characters trivial on torsion
items.statement: Let ψ: G_F → O^× be a character trivial on the torsion subgroup of G_F^ab. Then after replacing L by a finite extension there is a character η: G_F → O^× with η^d = ψ.

items.name: Conrad: crystalline characters of G_F
items.statement: Under the Artin map, a character ψ: F^× → O^× is crystalline if and only if ψ(x) = ∏_{σ: F→L} σ(x)^{n_σ} for all x ∈ O_F^× and some integers n_σ (Conrad, Lifting global representations with local properties, Proposition B.4).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 6.5–6.6, pp. 47–48 (arXiv v2 pp. 53–54)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory R06.2 plans D_cris and admissibility but does not state the classification of crystalline characters by Lubin–Tate characters.

items.name: Lemma 6.5: crystalline characters with prescribed restriction to torsion
items.statement: Let κ: G_F → O^× be a character. Then there is a crystalline character ψ: G_F → O^× such that ψκ^{−1} is trivial on the torsion subgroup of G_F^ab and ψ ≡ κ (mod ϖ). In particular, for characters κ̄: G_F → k^× and χ: μ_{p^∞}(F) → O^× there is a crystalline ψ: G_F → O^× lifting κ̄ with ψ(Art_F(z)) = χ(z) for all z ∈ μ_{p^∞}(F).
items.note: Corrected for source issue E7: the character ψ(x) = σ(xϖ_F^{−v(x)})^a of the proof has ψ(ϖ_F) = 1, so ψκ^{−1}(ϖ_F) = κ(ϖ_F)^{−1} need not be ≡ 1; multiplying ψ by the unramified character sending ϖ_F to κ(ϖ_F) gives the congruence, and the first statement is unchanged.

items.name: Lemma 6.6: the central character of M_∞ ⊗_{R_det,x} O and its algebraicity for crystalline ψ
items.statement: Let ψ: G_F → O^× lift det ρ̄ and x: R_{det ρ̄} → O the corresponding map. Then the centre Z of G acts on M_∞ ⊗_{R_{det ρ̄},x} O by δ^{−1}, where δ: Z ≅ F^× → G_F^ab → O^× is ε^{d(d−1)/2}ψ ∘ Art_F (ε the p-adic cyclotomic character); M_∞ ⊗_{R_{det ρ̄},x} O is non-zero and projective in the category of linearly compact O⟦K⟧-modules on which Z ∩ K acts by δ^{−1}; and if ψ is crystalline there is an algebraic character θ: Res^F_{Q_p} G_m → G_m over L with δ|_{K∩Z} equal to O_F^× → (Res^F_{Q_p} G_m)(Q_p) → (Res^F_{Q_p} G_m)(L) → G_m(L) via θ.

items.name: The modules M_∞(V), the set Irr(G) and the Banach representations Π(M)
items.statement: For a continuous representation V of K on a finite-dimensional L-vector space with a K-stable O-lattice Θ, M_∞(Θ) := (Hom^cont_{O⟦K⟧}(M_∞, Θ^d))^d with (·)^d = Hom^cont_O(·, O), a finitely generated R_∞-module, and M_∞(V) := M_∞(Θ) ⊗_O L, independent of Θ.
