Irr(G) is the set of isomorphism classes of irreducible algebraic representations of (Res^F_{Q_p} GL_d)_L, viewed as K-representations through K → (Res^F_{Q_p} GL_d)(L). For a compact O-module M, Π(M) := Hom^cont_O(M, L) with the supremum norm; for a compact O⟦K⟧-module it is a unitary L-Banach representation of K, and Π(O⟦K⟧) ≅ 𝒞(K, L) (Schneider–Teitelbaum, Corollary 2.2).

items.name: Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen: density of locally algebraic vectors of a given central character
items.statement: Let θ: Res^F_{Q_p} G_m → G_m be an algebraic character over L, τ ∈ Irr(G) with central character θ, and δ the associated character of Z ∩ K. For every non-zero K-stable direct summand Π of 𝒞_δ(K, L) (as Π(M) for M in Lemma 6.7), the evaluation map ⊕_{ξ' ∈ Irr(G/Z)} τ ⊗ ξ' ⊗ Hom^cont_K(τ ⊗ ξ', Π) → Π has dense image (Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen, Corollary 7.8, as applied in the proof of Lemma 6.7).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.7, p. 49 (arXiv v2 p. 54)
items.note: Imported; a prerequisite paper (arXiv:2012.01041, published in Selecta Math. 31 (2025)). The same density, for Π(M_∞), is the key point (35) of the proof of Theorem 6.1.

items.name: Lemma 6.7: non-zero projectives with algebraic central character see some algebraic representation
items.statement: Let θ: Res^F_{Q_p} G_m → G_m be an algebraic character over L and δ: Z ∩ K → O^× the character associated to θ as in Lemma 6.6. If M is non-zero and projective in the category of linearly compact O⟦K⟧-modules on which Z ∩ K acts by δ^{−1}, then there is ξ ∈ Irr(G) with Hom^cont_K(M, ξ^*) ≠ 0.

items.name: Emerton–Paškūnas: the closure of the supports of the M_∞(ξ) is a union of irreducible components
items.statement: The Zariski closure in Spec R_∞ of the union of the supports of the M_∞(ξ'), ξ' ∈ Irr(G), is a union of irreducible components of Spec R_∞ (Emerton–Paškūnas, Theorem 6.12, following Chenevier and Nakamura).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.8, p. 49 (arXiv v2 p. 55)
items.note: Imported from Emerton–Paškūnas, J. Éc. polytech. Math. 7 (2020); a prerequisite paper. Their Theorems 5.1 and 5.3 are the model for the proof of Theorem 6.1.

items.name: Theorem 6.8: R^□_ρ̄ acts faithfully on M_∞
items.statement: Assume p ∤ 2d (needed for M_∞ to exist). The action of R^□_ρ̄ on M_∞ is faithful.
items.locator: Theorem 6.8, p. 49 (arXiv v2 p. 55); Remarks 6.9–6.10, p. 50
items.note: Proof: each minimal prime of R^□_ρ̄ is the kernel of R^□_ρ̄ → R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ (Corollary 4.21); Lemma 6.5 gives a crystalline ψ with ψ ∘ Art_F = χ on μ, Lemmas 6.6–6.7 a ξ with M_∞(ξ) non-zero over x, Emerton–Paškūnas a minimal prime of R_∞ in the annihilator's support, Lemma 6.3 its image, and reducedness of R^□_ρ̄ (Corollary 4.22) concludes. Remark 6.9: whether R_∞ acts faithfully is open. Remark 6.10: the expectation that M_∞ realises p-adic local Langlands forces this theorem.

items.name: Theorem 6.1 (Theorem 1.6): Zariski density of crystalline, potentially crystabelline and potentially crystalline supercuspidal points
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a finite extension of Q_p with absolute Galois group G_F, L a finite extension of Q_p such that Hom_{Q_p-alg}(F, L) has [F:Q_p] elements, O its ring of integers, ϖ a uniformiser and k the residue field; let d ≥ 1 and ρ̄: G_F → GL_d(k) a continuous representation all of whose irreducible subquotients are absolutely irreducible, R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring, D̄ its pseudo-character (determinant law), R^ps the universal deformation ring of D̄ and R_{det ρ̄} the universal deformation ring of the character det ρ̄. Assume p ∤ 2d, and let Σ be any of Σ^cris, Σ^prnc_k or Σ^spcd_k (k regular). Then Σ is Zariski dense in X^□ = Spec R^□_ρ̄ (equivalently in Spec R^□_ρ̄[1/p]).
items.locator: Theorem 6.1, p. 46 (arXiv v2 p. 51); Theorem 1.6, p. 3; Remark 6.2, p. 46
items.note: Proved as Emerton–Paškūnas Theorems 5.1 and 5.3, with Theorem 6.8 in place of their faithfulness hypothesis. Remark 6.10: the sequel (Böckle–Iyengar–Paškūnas, PNAS 2023) proves density of Σ^cris in (Spf R^□_ρ̄)^rig for all p using the Emerton–Gee stack; Σ^prnc_k and Σ^spcd_k are not dense there, and this section is the only known method for them.
